newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul Bancorp non-performing assets cut.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul Bancorp non-performing assets cut.

text.p: St. Paul Bancorp Inc said Wednesday its non-performing assets as of December 31 were $12.5 million or 0.29 percent of total assets, the lowest level since the company went public in 1987.
This compares with non-performing assets of $20.6 million, or 0.48 percent of total assets, as of September 30, 1996, and $29.2 million, or 0.71 percent of total assets, as of December 31, 1995.
Earlier, St. Paul Bancorp reported fourth quarter results of $0.46 a share, up from $0.38 a year ago.

For the year, it earned $1.10 a share, including a $21.0 million charge, down from year-ago earnings of $1.49 a share. Excluding the charge for a Savings Association Insurance Fund assessment, St. Paul's earnings for 1996 would have been been $40.2 million or $1.69 a share, up 10 percent from a year ago.

"The improvement in earnings for the fourth quarter and the year reflects the results of our strategy to increase earning assets and to continue to improve other income," Joseph Scully, chairman, said in a statement. "We intend to continue this strategy in 1997, as weel as seek opportunities to expand St. Paul's franchise in the chicago area by the opening of additional in-store or storefront branches."
